TWO STREAMS. WORK YOU CAN SHOW.

A shared foundation. Two areas of depth.

Both streams use AI as a development partner and require the learner to review code, test results, protect data and explain the solution. The distinction is the depth of responsibility.

01

Frame a real problem

Define the user, scope and a useful outcome that can be tested.

02

Build with accountability

Use AI and code with review, debugging, version control and documented decisions.

03

Develop an evidence portfolio

Show the brief, working demo, contribution history, test results, feedback and handover.

04

Explore relevant work

Develop capability for suitable permanent, contract or freelance opportunities; selection depends on demonstrated skills and role requirements.

CHOOSE YOUR AREA OF DEPTH

Two streams.
Two clear responsibilities.

Both build working software. One goes deeper into AI behaviour; the other into the complete application.

STREAM 01

AI Application Developer

Make AI useful, reliable and controlled.

  1. Frame the task, approved data and success checks.
  2. Develop prompts, model API calls and predictable output formats.
  3. Retrieve approved knowledge and support answers with citations.
  4. Connect tools with permissions, human approval and recovery paths.
  5. Evaluate answer quality, security, response time and model usage cost.
  6. Build, deploy and monitor a usable AI application.
Example outcome

A policy assistant that cites approved sources and routes uncertain cases to staff.

STREAM 02

AI-powered Full-Stack Developer

Build the complete application people use.

  1. Map user journeys, application behaviour and data.
  2. Build accessible screens, forms and mobile-friendly interfaces.
  3. Implement business rules, APIs, SQL records, sign-in and permissions.
  4. Integrate AI where it improves the user’s task.
  5. Test complete flows, data changes, permissions and failure cases.
  6. Deploy, maintain and improve the application using logs and feedback.
Example outcome

A returns portal with customer screens, staff approval, records and a policy assistant.

THE COMMON FOUNDATION

Experience you can explain. Evidence you can show.

Both streams start with a real user, a defined problem and a useful outcome. AI supports the work; you remain responsible for reviewing, testing and explaining it.

01

Problem & working demo

Show the brief, scope, deployed solution and main user task.

02

Code & contribution

Explain your Git history, decisions and the parts you built or changed.

03

Tests & feedback

Present quality results, difficult cases, revisions and remaining limits.

04

Responsible handover

Document setup, permissions, data handling and operating notes.
